# Results — Study 166 (First-Five-Days) on real annual ^GSPC tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  The First-Five-Days Early Warning System (Stock Trader's Almanac): does the sign of the S&P 500's return over the first 5 trading days of January predict the full-year direction?  ^GSPC daily history from 1950, annual first-five-days and full-year returns derived from daily closes (log-returns).  As-of **2026-06-15**.  n = **76 years** (1950-2025) — tiny effective n, a key caveat throughout.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (annual series) | 1950-2025 (76 years) | `04a2745a0f8a` |

*Derived from daily closes; first-five-days return = log(close on 5th trading day of Jan / close on last trading day of prior Dec); full-year return = log(Dec year-end close / prior Dec year-end close).  No look-ahead: F5D signal formed after the 5th trading day.*

## Test 1 — Hit-rate vs base rate

The raw hit-rate (sign(F5D) == sign(full-year)) is **69.7 %** on 76 years.  Against a fair-coin null (50 %) that is statistically significant (binomial p = 0.0004).  But the market drifts up most years — the **unconditional full-year positive rate is 73.7 %** — so the relevant null is not a coin but *knowing that equity markets trend up*.  Against that base rate the hit-rate of 69.7 % is *below* it, and the one-sided binomial p-value is **0.8200**.  The indicator does not beat the base rate.

| Test | Hit-rate | p-value | Conclusion |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| vs a coin (50 %) | **69.7 %** | **0.0004** | Significant against a coin |
| vs base rate (73.7 %) | 69.7 % | 0.8200 | **Not significant vs base rate** |

- Up-F5D hit-rate: **83.7 %** (49 years) — but the base rate for those years is high.
- Down-F5D hit-rate: **44.4 %** (27 years) — the indicator correctly calls a down full-year only 44.4 % of the time.
- Permutation p-value (random-label control): **0.0080** — borderline.

## Test 2 — Mean contrast (up-F5D vs down-F5D full-year returns)

| F5D sign | n | Mean full-year return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Up F5D | 49 | **+12.51 %** | — |
| Down F5D | 27 | **-0.44 %** | — |
| **Contrast (up − dn)** | 76 | **+12.95 %** | **+4.87** |

The contrast is **economically large (12.95 %)** and statistically significant (HAC *t* = 4.87, Welsh p = 0.0011).  However, this reflects two known confounds: (1) the F5D return *is part of* the full-year return (5 days of overlap), creating a mechanical correlation; (2) up-F5D years tend to be bull-market regimes where both January and December-year-end land high.  Regime correlation, not genuine early-warning.

## Sub-period stability — the signal weakens post-1985

| Period | n | Hit-rate | Contrast | HAC t | p (coin) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1950–1985 | 36 | 80.6 % | +16.2 % | +4.88 | 0.0002 |
| 1986–2025 | 40 | 60.0 % | +9.9 % | +2.90 | 0.1341 |

Post-1985 the hit-rate drops to 60.0 % (not significant vs a coin, p = 0.1341) and the contrast (9.9 %) — while still above the inference bar (HAC t = 2.90) — is weaker than the earlier period.  The pattern of a pre-publication strong effect that softens post-discovery is consistent with either statistical luck in the discovery sample or gradual arbitrage.

## F5D strategy vs buy-and-hold

| Arm | Mean/yr | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| F5D strategy (long if up-F5D, flat if dn-F5D), 10 bp cost | 8.01 % | 0.668 |
| Buy-and-hold full year | 7.91 % | 0.489 |

The F5D strategy slightly **outperforms buy-and-hold on mean return** (8.01 % vs 7.91 %/yr) and on Sharpe.  But this edge is largely driven by the pre-1985 data.  The strategy sits flat in 27 out of 76 years; in approximately 15 of those, the full year was still positive — the strategy missed real gains.  Post-1985 the tactical value is marginal.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.**  The indicator beats a coin (hit-rate 69.7 %, p = 0.0004) but **not the base rate** (p = 0.8200).  The large HAC t = 4.87 is inflated by mechanical overlap (F5D is part of the full year) and regime correlation.  Post-1985 the directional hit-rate (60.0 %) is not significant vs a coin (p = 0.1341).  Effective n = 76 is tiny.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  The strategy marginally outperforms buy-and-hold (8.01 % vs 7.91 %/yr) but the signal is not robust enough post-1985 and the outperformance is within noise at n = 76.
- **Beats a coin? — NONE.**  Beats a fair coin (p = 0.0004) but not the correct null (base rate 73.7 %, p = 0.8200).  The almanac's 'famous accuracy' is mostly the equity premium in calendar clothing.
